problem: Consider the function $f(x)=3\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$ If the critical points of $f(x)$ for $x\in (-\pi ,\pi )$ are $x={x}_{1}$ and $x={x}_{2},$ what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}?$

Consider the function $f(x)=\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$ In **ascending order**, the **exact values** of the critical points of $f(x)$ for $x\in (-\pi ,\pi )$ are

feedback.worked_solution:
A critical point of $f(x)$ is a point $x=c$ in the domain of $f$ such that either ${f}^{′}(c)=0$ or ${f}^{′}(c)$ does not exist.

Differentiating $f(x),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\  & =\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-3\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

We now proceed to find the critical points:

- First, we compute the points where ${f}^{′}(c)=0.$ We set the derivative equal to zero, and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-3\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =0 \\ \sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡x & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =arctan\,(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}})+n\pi  \\  & =\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $-\pi <x<\pi .$

- setting $n=-1$ gives $x=-\frac{5\pi }{6},$

- setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{6}.$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $-\pi <x<\pi .$ So, the solutions to this equation for $x\in (-\pi ,\pi )$ are 

$$
x=-\frac{5\pi }{6},\,x=\frac{\pi }{6}.
$$

Therefore, $f(x)$ has stationary points at $x=-\frac{5\pi }{6}$ and $x=\frac{\pi }{6}.$

- Second, we note that ${f}^{′}(x)$ exists for all values of $x\in (-\pi ,\pi ).$ So $f(x)$ has no non-stationary critical points.

Therefore, in ascending order, the critical points of $f(x)$ for $x\in (-\pi ,\pi )$ are 

$$
x=-\frac{5\pi }{6}\,\text{and}\,x=\frac{\pi }{6}.
$$
